quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs use yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs use orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move your vehicle out of the way, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle out of the way, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Proceed slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and wait. Only move when a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and look for other drivers. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What can you do at a flashing yellow arrow traffic light?

options.text: Go in the direction of the arrow after coming to a complete stop.
Go in the direction of the arrow after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.
Go in the direction of the arrow at your current speed because you have the right-of-way.
Stop and wait until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go in the direction of the arrow after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you may go in that direction, but first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Stop to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.question: When is passing prohibited?

options.text: On hills and curves.
At intersections.
At railroad crossings.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: Your view to the side is blocked at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: When your view is blocked at an intersection, stop first. Then inch forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.
Yes, it is a distraction.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This is dangerous.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as cars.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular cars.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than regular cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely, you may crash into them if they stop suddenly. Keep enough distance to stop safely.

questions.question: On the interstate, when should you use the left lane?

options.text: To exit.
To pass another vehicle.
Before crossing the median.

questions.correctAnswerText: To pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane on the interstate. Use the left lane only to pass other vehicles. Do not speed when passing.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a serious crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When you stop your car on the roadside for an emergency, you do not need to set the parking brake.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always set your parking brake during an emergency stop. Turn on your emergency lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Does driving speed affect how far your car travels when you brake?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Speed does affect braking distance. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
Areas behind the truck where cars have plenty of space.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars disappear from view or are too close. Cars in these areas greatly increase the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about drinking and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight, you can safely drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, driving is safe.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs judgment. You need good judgment to react safely on the road. Any amount of alcohol can affect your driving, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person's body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include sex, how much food they have eaten, and how much they have drunk. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check several times if needed. Watch traffic in front of you and in the next lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle will hit if it crashes.

questions.question: Your following distance behind a motorcycle should:

options.text: Be the same as for any other vehicle.
Decrease.
Increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Keep more distance behind a motorcycle than behind other vehicles. Motorcycles can stop and turn much faster than larger vehicles. You need extra time to react to their quick movements.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass if it is safe to do so.
